title: runtime-contract-enforcer: add strict response_format validation with tool-call fence and streaming fallback
author: Evelyn Cho
description: Motivation: Customers running structured output with strict mode and tool-calls reported intermittent schema violation errors during streaming reconnections and partial tool-call handoffs. This PR introduces a lightweight runtime "contract enforcer" that validates the outgoing response against the requested response_format (JSON schema / shape hint), enforces a tool-call fence to prevent mid-call schema violations, and provides a controlled streaming fallback that can gracefully close and rewind the stream when the model produces unrecoverable schema drift. Design summary: - New runtime layer `contract_enforcer` sits between the generation runtime and the OpenAI-compatibility middleware. It receives the negotiated response_format schema (if any) and maintains a small validation state per-request to allow non-destructive streaming validation checks. - Tool-call fencing: when a function/tool call is declared in the response contract, the enforcer prevents interleaving partial JSON tokens from being interpreted as tool call boundaries; it emits clear failure codes when the model outputs data that would cause ambiguous tool invocation. - Streaming fallback: if validation fails mid-stream and cannot be fixed by coercion, the enforcer signals a controlled stream termination with a machine-readable error chunk and a short rewind token that clients and the OpenAI compat layer can use to request an immediate re-run or a non-streaming error payload. - OpenAI-compat changes: the middleware now maps contract enforcer error codes to OpenAI-style error responses (with improved error_message details) and supports `X-Redwood-Contract-Rewind` header for retries. Checklist: - [x] Implement core contract_enforcer runtime and attach to request pipeline - [x] Add schema coercion heuristics (soft coercion for permissive mode) - [x] Add tool-call fence with explicit error codes - [x] Emit streaming error chunk + rewind token on unrecoverable failures - [x] Update openai_compat middleware to map error codes and headers - [x] Unit tests for validator, tool-call fence, header mappings - [x] Integration tests for streaming rewind and non-stream fallback - [x] Update docs: API reference for response_format strict mode and error codes - [x] Benchmarked perf impact (micro-benchmark in perf-canary) Commits (high level): - feat(contract_enforcer): new runtime module + validation state machine - feat(openai_compat): map enforcer errors and add rewind header - fix(streaming): make buffer checkpoints reentrant and add a max-checkpoint cap - test: add unit/integration tests for tool-call fencing and streaming fallback - docs: API reference for error codes and usage examples Changed areas (high level): - runtime/contract_enforcer/{enforcer.py,validator.py,errors.py} (new) - middleware/openai_compat/contract_mapping.py (update) - serving/streaming/checkpoint.py (update to support rewind token) - api/docs/response_contracts.md (new section) - tests/{unit,test_integration_contracts}.py (new) Migration notes: This change is opt-in behind `response_contract_enforcer` feature flag in runtime config. Default behavior remains unchanged for customers not using response_format strict mode. Backwards compatibility: The OpenAI compatibility layer will translate enforcer errors to OpenAI-style errors so existing clients continue to receive familiar shapes, but with additional `x-redwood-*` headers and a new `contract_error_code` field in JSON error bodies. Operational notes: - Enforcer adds a small CPU cost and modest memory for per-request state; micro-benchmarks show ~4% median latency increase at p95 for strict mode on a <256 token sequence. We will start rollout to Dedicated customers only and monitor via perf-canary dashboards. - If regressions are observed, we can disable the feature flag per-cluster. CI: All checks passed on the final run (unit + integration + lint + mypy + perf-canary smoke). Merge: squash and merge.

review_conversation: Reviewer Marco Alvarez: 'Overall design looks good. Two concerns: 1) we need explicit limits on rewind token lifetime to avoid replay amplification, 2) please add more unit tests around nested tool-call sequences.' Author reply (Evelyn): 'Added limit config (max_rewind_ttl_seconds) and extended test coverage to nested tool-call cases.' Reviewer Priya Natarajan: 'Can we ensure we don't change existing response headers unless the feature flag is enabled?' Author: 'Yes — new headers are only emitted when the feature flag is on. Confirmed in middleware mapping.' Reviewer Jonas Becker: 'Benchmarks look acceptable; please add a canary dashboard alert if p95 climbs >10%.' Author: 'Added dashboard and alert rule in perf-canary.' Final status: Approved by all reviewers and passing CI.
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in 'contract_enforcer' runtime to validate response_format schemas at runtime, tool-call fencing to prevent ambiguous tool invocations, and a controlled streaming fallback with machine-readable error chunks and a rewind token. Opt-in via runtime feature flag. OpenAI-compat layer maps new error codes to existing error shapes and exposes retry headers.
